comparisons.peer_topic: Client CPU product launches and performance
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Intel launched Intel Core Ultra Series 1 (first with integrated NPU for AI workloads) and the power-efficient Intel Core Ultra 200V Series. Additionally, the 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors continued to serve a significant majority of client sales.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures identify the 2024 market entry of 'AI PCs' driven by new client processor architectures with integrated AI accelerators. Intel states that the 'Intel Core Ultra Series 1' introduced the 'first AI PCs to the market' in 2024 with an integrated neural processing unit, mirroring Qualcomm's disclosure of AI-focused PCs launching in 2024 powered by its Snapdragon platforms.

sentences.text: For example, a new class of AI-focused PCs, including those powered by our Snapdragon X Series platforms, launched in 2024, allowing for increased productivity and enhanced use cases enabled by on-device AI processing at low power.

▪Client CPUs. In 2024, we ramped sales of the Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload. The Intel Core Ultra Series 1, manufactured on the Intel 4 process, introduced the first AI PCs to the market. We also launched the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series, showcasing power efficiency and long-lasting battery life. The 200V Series, manufactured by an external foundry, leverages our Xe2 GPU architecture, bringing improved efficiency, second-generation ray tracing units and XMX AI acceleration to thin and light notebooks. During 2024, a significant majority of our client sales consisted of our 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, manufactured on Intel 7, which allow us to serve the breadth of customer and computing needs in the client market.

comparisons.peer_topic: PC market and AI-driven DRAM demand
comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs feature AI capabilities and high-performance neural processing chipsets, leading to significantly higher DRAM content, with the company announcing low-power compression-attached memory modules to support AI workloads on PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies attribute the advancement of next-generation PCs to AI capabilities, noting the resulting hardware implications. While Qualcomm focuses on the 'increased productivity and enhanced use cases enabled by on-device AI processing,' Micron emphasizes the supply-side impact, stating that PCs with 'high-performance neural processing chipsets' will have 'significantly more DRAM content.'
